searchText: A basic question regarding Ethereum clients. Are they required to maintain a full Merkle Tree for the entire state? or Do they maintain a partial tree? You need a full tree to calculate the state root every block. Can such a big tree be stored in RAM? Depends on how much RAM you have. 😄 To calculate the state root, you only actually need the mutated branches, which is a *much* smaller set than the full tree. So one can imagine a design where you keep the recently touched set of branches in RAM or something, and you only go to disk when you need to read in a new one. That being said, for failure recovery you *do* want to constantly be writing updates to disk. Maybe you only write every 100th update to disk though, since you can just re-execute the last 100 transactions on failure recovery. Hmm... Thanks... I guess Erigon approach is a little different.., Or is it? We maintain the upper part of the Merkle-Patrcia trie in the DB.
